about: Labels given by the user looking at the images. Ground truth for the test pool. Filenames are uninformative or deliberately wrong and were not used: three files named LIPSS turned out to be nanoparticle films.
source: user, one at a time for 1-6, then in one pass over the survey

labels.label: calibration grating
labels.note: Certified pitch, so this is the reference the periodicity measurement itself is checked against. Grating model not yet confirmed.

labels.label: scalpel scratch through a film, for film thickness
labels.note: User: 'misura molto frequente'. Two height levels (bimodality 0.51, kurtosis -1.0). Periodicity 28 is a false positive: one straight edge, not a repeat.

labels.label: halide perovskite crystal on a flat substrate
labels.note: Faceted crystal ~5 x 15 um. User: the curved background is the z feedback landing/flying over the tall crystal, not sample shape -- this is the artifact to correct.

labels.label: pitted surface, genuine morphology (material not named)
labels.note: User confirmed the image is good and everything in it is sample. I wrongly called the edge streaks a tip artifact.

labels.label: same sample as 4, different area
labels.note: Descriptors land far apart despite the same specimen: RMS 51 vs 23 nm, correlation 566 vs 234 nm, skewness -0.37 vs -1.97.

labels.label: wide view of the sample in 4 and 5
labels.note: At 176 nm/pixel the pits that filled 5-20 pixels at 5 um now occupy one or two. Shape is gone below the pixel.
Not labelled by the user. Fibrous texture and pits, resembles 4-6.
Not labelled by the user. Pitted surface with a noise change on one scan line at y = 11.5 um.

labels.label: edge of a film, with an unexpected object (dirt) on it
labels.note: User: 'il bordo di un film, con un oggetto imprevisto (sporco). e' parziale'. The bright blob is contamination, not structure.
Not labelled. Densely pitted, skewness -1.51.
Not labelled. Pitted with a branching network of narrow channels.
Not labelled. Read as an optical disc surface: parallel diagonal tracks with aligned pits. The most periodic image in the pool, and the one where the periodicity measure fails worst.

labels.label: nanoparticle film
labels.note: User: partial, same as 14, a nanoparticle film. The filename says LIPSS and there is nothing periodic in it.

labels.label: nanoparticle film
labels.note: User linked it to 13. Filename says LIPSS; no periodicity measurable at 78 nm/pixel.

labels.label: film of spherical nanoparticles
labels.note: User: 'si film di nanoparticelle sferiche'. Filename says LIPSS.

labels.label: nanocellulose fragments on mica
labels.note: Background order chosen is 1 where 2 is right: order 1 explains 34%, order 2 explains 88%. The only clear under-fit in the pool.

labels.label: nanocellulose fragments on mica
labels.note: RMS 0.9 nm, the flattest scan in the pool. Row banding 0.913, the highest: rows must be aligned before any counting.

labels.label: spherical nanoparticles on silicon
labels.note: User: 'probabilmente qualche artefatto per la punta deformata'. The cleanest 'objects above a flat background' case in the pool, skewness +1.43.

labels.label: dense oxide structure -- the rounded shapes are grains
labels.note: User: 'fitta struttura di un ossido penso, quelli sono i grani, possibile effetto convoluzione dovuto alla geometria della punta'.

labels.label: dense oxide structure, grains
labels.note: Two single-row bright glitches at y = 16.5 and 21 um are acquisition artifacts.

labels.label: dense oxide structure, zoomed in
labels.note: Background order 0 is probably right: there is no background here, only objects.

labels.label: discard
labels.note: User: 'scarta'. Too little of the frame survives to be worth cropping.

labels.label: scratch on a film
labels.note: User: 'scratch su film, scansione incompleta quindi croppa e misura'. Same measurement family as index 2.

labels.label: scratch on a film
labels.note: Crop, then measure the step as film thickness.

labels.label: 2D perovskite nanosheet on a TEM grid
labels.note: The regular dot lattice is the TEM GRID, i.e. the support, not the sample. A periodic structure in an image does not have to belong to the specimen.

labels.label: very well defined nanoparticles
labels.note: User: 'nanoparticelle molto ben definite, scansione interrotta'.

labels.label: close-packed nanosphere monolayer
labels.note: User confirmed the reading. Spheres ~120 nm touching; the object count reports 4 pieces because there is no background to stand above.

labels.label: packed spheres, larger and in several layers
labels.note: User confirmed the reading.

labels.label: duplicate of 28
labels.note: Same area rescanned.

labels.label: polished substrate, probably metal
labels.note: User: 'ci hai preso, metallo forse, altro polished'. Object count claims 18.8% of the frame -- a false positive inside the noise.

labels.label: duplicate of 30
labels.note: Same area rescanned.
